title: KERNEL adaptive execution classification
description: The compact, inspectable representation of how KERNEL chose to execute a task. Three independent dimensions: domain, work_shape, safety. Surfaced to the user only via /kernel:status or /kernel:why.

domain.description: What kind of work this is. Selects which domain pack loads. Extensible: a domain pack may register additional values.

work_shape.description: How much process the work needs. Independent of domain and safety.

safety.description: How much protection the work needs. Independent of domain and work_shape.

confidence.description: Classifier confidence in this routing. Below low_confidence_floor the router must state its uncertainty rather than proceed silently.

reasons.description: The evidence that drove classification. Each entry must be a checkable observation about the task, not a restatement of the verdict.

escalate_when.description: Named conditions that move work to a heavier shape or higher safety. Required for direct and gated shapes: a mode with no exit condition cannot adapt.

deescalate_when.description: Named conditions that move work to a lighter shape. Required for gated and trajectory: a mode with no exit is a permanent operating system, which the brief rejects.

packs.description: Domain packs actually loaded for this task. Empty means universal core only.

verification.description: Domain-appropriate verification method chosen. Never hardcoded to 'tests'.

ownership.description: Writer/resource ownership claim for collision prevention.

announced.description: Whether this classification was surfaced to the user. True only when the mode materially changed behavior.

transient.description: True when this request is a lightweight subrequest that must not replace the active live-run route.

transitions.description: Append-only record of mode changes during the task, with the evidence that triggered each.

allOf.$comment: R1: any shape that is not the heaviest must name how it escalates. Without an exit condition a mode cannot adapt to reality.
R2: any shape heavier than direct must name how it de-escalates. Trajectory is a gear, not the permanent operating system.
R3: protected work must name the verification that distinguishes the safe outcome from the unsafe one.
